descriptionChirho: The state of being free, especially freedom from the bondage of sin and the law, as proclaimed in Pauline theology (Gal 2:4, 5:1, 5:13; 2 Cor 3:17) and the epistle of James (Jas 1:25, 2:12). Both clusters represent the same abstract noun in different grammatical cases: nominative/accusative/dative (S66948) and genitive (S66949). Multilingual translations confirm a single concept: Spanish 'libertad/de libertad,' Hindi 'स्वतन्त्रता/स्वतन्त्रता–की,' Arabic 'حُرّيَّةِ/الحُرِّيَّةِ,' Korean '자유를/자유–의,' Swahili 'uhuru/ya-uhuru.' No semantic split is warranted—only case morphology distinguishes these groups.
